outline.description: This chapter introduces the core concept of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT), contrasting it with traditional tokenization-based LLMs. It sets the pedagogical stage by explaining why current models rely on static vocabularies and outlines the proposal's fundamental shift toward dynamic, entropy-based computation allocation.
subtopics: The limitations of fixed-vocabulary tokenization (BPE, SFT)
Why byte-level modeling is inefficient at scale (sequence length explosion)
The BLT Thesis: Dynamic compute allocation based on information complexity
Overview of the Patch-Based Architecture vs. Token-Based Architecture
Learning without fixed vocabularies: From language modeling to byte visualization

outline.description: Dedicated to the mechanism of 'Patching'—the process of converting raw byte streams into variable-length latent units. This chapter provides a comprehensive guide to different heuristics for segmenting data.
subtopics: Static Patching: The Strided Approach (The Baseline Method)
Whitespace Patching: Leveraging syntactic boundaries in text
Entropy Patching: A Data-Driven Approach Using Byte Level LM Predictions
Computational Calculation of Next-Byte Entropy ($H(x_i)$) and Patch Boundaries
Incremental vs. Non-Incremental Patching: The Critical Role of Future Context Prediction
Comparison of Techniques: Space vs. Dynamic vs. Static in Practice

outline.description: A deep dive into the specific components of the Byte Latent Transformer model. This chapter breaks down the hybrid architecture that allows efficient mapping between raw bytes and high-dimensional latent patches.
subtopics: Global Latent Transformer ($	extbf{G}$): The Core Computation Engine

* Cross-Attention Mechanisms for Latent Representation Pooling
